valeur-venale.definition: Estimated price at which a property could be sold under normal market conditions, between willing and sufficiently informed parties, at a given date.
valeur-venale.title: Market value of a property: definition and valuation
valeur-venale.description: What the market value (valeur vénale) of a property means and the main criteria used to estimate it.

surface-habitable.definition: Built floor area after deducting the space taken up by walls, partitions, steps, stairwells, ducts and door and window recesses, according to the regulatory rules. Some areas are excluded.
surface-habitable.title: Living area (surface habitable): definition and calculation
surface-habitable.description: How the French living area is defined, the main deductions and how it differs from the Carrez area.

surface-carrez.definition: Private floor area calculated under the rules of the Carrez law for the co-ownership units concerned. It does not necessarily match the living area.
surface-carrez.title: Carrez law: definition of the private floor area
surface-carrez.description: How the Carrez area is defined and when it must be stated in the sale of a co-ownership unit in France.

dpe.definition: Document assessing the energy performance of a home and its greenhouse gas emissions. It assigns ratings from A to G under the applicable regulatory method.
dpe.title: DPE (energy performance certificate): definition and ratings
dpe.description: Understand the French DPE, its energy ratings and its role when a home is sold or let.

audit-energetique.definition: Study analysing the energy characteristics of a building and proposing works scenarios to improve its energy performance. Whether it is mandatory depends on the situation and the rules in force.
audit-energetique.title: Energy audit: definition and purpose
audit-energetique.description: What an energy audit is for and in which situations it may be required when a property is sold in France.

compromis-de-vente.definition: Pre-contract by which the seller and the buyer mutually commit to complete the sale, subject to the conditions set out in the contract.
compromis-de-vente.title: Compromis de vente (preliminary sale agreement): definition
compromis-de-vente.description: The role of the French preliminary sale agreement, its conditions precedent and the steps before the final deed.

acte-authentique-de-vente.term: Notarial deed of sale (acte authentique de vente)
acte-authentique-de-vente.definition: Legal deed received and signed before a notary that formalises the property sale and the transfer of ownership on the agreed terms.
acte-authentique-de-vente.title: Notarial deed of sale (acte authentique): definition
acte-authentique-de-vente.description: The notary’s role and the main steps in signing the final notarial deed of sale in France.

condition-suspensive.definition: Clause making the final completion of a contract dependent on a specified event, such as obtaining a mortgage.
condition-suspensive.title: Condition precedent (condition suspensive) in real estate
condition-suspensive.description: How a condition precedent works in a French property pre-contract and what effects it can have.

frais-acquisition.definition: All the costs linked to buying a property, including in particular duties and taxes, the notary’s fees and certain administrative costs.
frais-acquisition.title: Property purchase costs (frais de notaire): definition
frais-acquisition.description: What property purchase costs include in France, often called notary fees, and how to estimate them.

mandat-de-vente.definition: Contract by which an owner entrusts a real estate professional with marketing the property under the terms defined in the mandate.
mandat-de-vente.title: Sale mandate (mandat de vente): definition
mandat-de-vente.description: The role of a sale mandate, the obligations it sets out and the main types of mandate in France.

honoraires-agence.definition: Remuneration owed to a real estate professional for the services set out in the mandate. The amount and who pays it must be stated in line with the applicable rules.
honoraires-agence.title: Real estate agency fees: definition
honoraires-agence.description: What agency fees cover and why it must be clearly stated who pays them.

terrain-constructible.definition: Land on which construction may be authorised under the applicable planning rules. Whether it can be built on depends in particular on the zoning, the regulations, easements and the characteristics of the land.
terrain-constructible.title: Building land: definition and checks
terrain-constructible.description: The main points to check before buying a plot advertised as building land in France.

emprise-au-sol.definition: Vertical projection of the volume of a building, including overhangs and projections as defined by planning rules. It can be used to assess what may be built on a plot.
emprise-au-sol.title: Building footprint (emprise au sol): planning definition
emprise-au-sol.description: How the building footprint is defined and its role in assessing a construction project.

plan-local-urbanisme.definition: Planning document that sets out, among other things, the land-use rules, the zones and the requirements applying to construction or development projects.
plan-local-urbanisme.title: PLU (local urban plan): definition and planning rules
plan-local-urbanisme.description: What the French local urban plan is for and how it can affect a property project.

copropriete.definition: Legal organisation of a building whose ownership is shared between several people, each holding one or more units made up of a private part and a share of the common parts.
copropriete.title: Co-ownership (copropriété): definition and how it works
copropriete.description: The principles of co-ownership, the difference between private and common parts and the role of the managing agent.

charges-copropriete.definition: Expenses for the upkeep, maintenance and administration of the common parts and for shared services and equipment. How they are split depends on the applicable rules.
charges-copropriete.title: Co-ownership service charges: definition
charges-copropriete.description: What co-ownership service charges cover and how they are split between co-owners.

servitude.definition: Burden placed on a property for the benefit of another property or, in some cases, arising from legal or administrative provisions. It may concern, for example, a right of way or utility networks.
servitude.title: Easement (servitude): definition and examples
servitude.description: What a property easement is and how it can affect the use of land or a building.

credit-immobilier.definition: Loan granted to finance the purchase or construction of a property or certain works on it.
credit-immobilier.title: Mortgage (crédit immobilier): definition and how it works
credit-immobilier.description: How a mortgage works and the main points to examine before committing.

capacite-emprunt.definition: Amount a lender might agree to finance, based in particular on income, outgoings, the loan term and the applicable lending criteria.
capacite-emprunt.title: Mortgage borrowing capacity: definition
capacite-emprunt.description: The main factors that determine how much you can borrow to buy a property.

rendement-locatif-brut.definition: Ratio between the theoretical annual rent and the purchase price used, expressed as a percentage. This indicator does not take all charges and taxes into account.
rendement-locatif-brut.title: Gross rental yield: definition and calculation
rendement-locatif-brut.description: How gross rental yield is calculated and its limits when comparing investments.

vacance-locative.definition: Period during which a home intended for letting has no tenant and therefore generates no rent.
vacance-locative.title: Rental vacancy: definition and impact on yield
vacance-locative.description: What rental vacancy is and how it affects the income and yield of a property investment.

bail-habitation.definition: Lease of a home governed by the legal regime that applies to its use and to the situation of the parties.
bail-habitation.title: Residential lease: definition and obligations
bail-habitation.description: The principles of a French residential lease and the essential obligations of landlord and tenant.

logement-decent.definition: Housing that meets the legal criteria on safety, health, minimum comfort and energy performance.
logement-decent.title: Decent housing: definition and criteria
logement-decent.description: The decency criteria a rented home must meet in France and why they matter.

garantie-decennale.definition: Statutory guarantee that can cover, for ten years, certain defects that undermine the soundness of a building or make it unfit for its purpose, under the conditions laid down by law.
garantie-decennale.title: Ten-year builder warranty (garantie décennale)
garantie-decennale.description: The principles of the French ten-year builder warranty and the defects it may cover.

vefa.definition: Contract by which the buyer purchases a property that is to be built or under construction. The transfer of ownership follows the statutory regime for this type of transaction.
vefa.title: VEFA: definition of an off-plan sale
vefa.description: How a VEFA (off-plan sale) works and the main steps in buying a new-build home in France.

viager.definition: Property transaction in which the price may consist of an initial lump sum (bouquet) and a periodic annuity paid to the seller, on the terms set in the contract.
viager.title: Viager (life annuity sale): definition and how it works
viager.description: The principles of a viager sale: the lump sum, the annuity and the main forms of this transaction.

plus-value-immobiliere.definition: Positive difference between the sale price of a property and its purchase price as adjusted under the applicable tax rules. The taxable amount may include costs, expenses and allowances provided for by law.
plus-value-immobiliere.title: Capital gain on property: definition and calculation
plus-value-immobiliere.description: What a capital gain on property is and the items that can enter into its tax calculation.

etat-des-risques.definition: Document providing information on certain risks and pollution to which a property may be exposed, in line with the obligations that apply to a sale or a letting.
etat-des-risques.title: Risk disclosure statement (état des risques): definition
etat-des-risques.description: The role of the risk disclosure statement and what it may contain for a sale or a letting in France.

notaire.definition: Public officer responsible in particular for receiving certain authentic deeds and for advising and ensuring legal certainty, especially in property transactions.
notaire.title: Notary: role in a property sale
notaire.description: The notary’s role in a French property transaction, from preparing the deeds to the final signing.

surface-de-plancher.definition: Regulatory area used in particular in planning, calculated from enclosed and covered areas with a ceiling height above 1.80 m, after the deductions laid down in the French Planning Code.
surface-de-plancher.title: Floor area (surface de plancher): planning definition
surface-de-plancher.description: How the planning floor area is defined and how it differs from the living area.

acompte.definition: Sum paid on account of the price or amount due, under the terms of the contract. In real estate, its effect depends in particular on the nature of the commitment and the contract terms.
acompte.title: Advance payment in real estate: definition and precautions
acompte.description: What an advance payment (acompte) is and what to check before paying one.

acte-sous-seing-prive.definition: Deed drawn up and signed by the parties without being received by a public officer. Its effect and the formalities required depend on the deed concerned and the applicable texts.
acte-sous-seing-prive.title: Private agreement (acte sous seing privé): definition
acte-sous-seing-prive.description: The difference between a private agreement and an authentic deed in a property transaction.

acquisition-en-viager.term: Buying a property en viager (acquisition en viager)
acquisition-en-viager.definition: Purchase of a property whose price may consist of a lump sum (bouquet) and a life annuity paid to the seller, on the agreed terms and under the applicable rules.
acquisition-en-viager.title: Buying en viager: how it works
acquisition-en-viager.description: The main elements of a viager purchase and what the lump sum and the annuity mean.

acquereur-non-professionnel.definition: Person who buys a property outside any professional real estate activity. This status can have legal consequences depending on the transaction and the applicable texts.
acquereur-non-professionnel.title: Non-professional buyer: definition
acquereur-non-professionnel.description: What being a non-professional buyer means in a French property transaction.

amiante.definition: Fibrous material formerly used in many building products, whose inhalation can pose health risks. Survey obligations depend in particular on the age of the building and the transaction.
amiante.title: Asbestos in a home: definition and surveys
amiante.description: Why an asbestos survey may be required for a sale, a letting or building works.

annonce-immobiliere.definition: Presentation of a property for sale or rent, usually including its description, main features, price or rent and the applicable regulatory information.
annonce-immobiliere.title: Property listing: essential information
annonce-immobiliere.description: The information a property listing should give and what to check before contacting the advertiser.

apport-personnel.definition: Money the buyer has available and puts towards part of the property project, possibly alongside a loan.
apport-personnel.title: Deposit (apport personnel): definition
apport-personnel.description: The role of the buyer’s own deposit in financing a property purchase.

architecte.definition: Regulated professional involved in particular in architectural design and, depending on the assignment, in overseeing a construction or renovation project.
architecte.title: Architect: role in a property project
architecte.description: The architect’s role and the situations in which hiring one may be required in France.

assainissement-collectif.definition: System in which waste water is carried to a public collection network and then treated by a suitable facility.
assainissement-collectif.title: Mains sewerage (assainissement collectif): definition
assainissement-collectif.description: How mains sewerage works and the useful checks when buying a property.

assainissement-non-collectif.definition: Individual installation for collecting and treating domestic waste water from a home that is not connected to the public sewer network.
assainissement-non-collectif.title: Private sewage system (ANC): definition
assainissement-non-collectif.description: The principles of individual sewage treatment and the inspections to plan for depending on the property.

attestation-de-propriete.definition: Document drawn up in particular in an inheritance or a notarial formality to record the transfer or holding of property rights, depending on the context.
attestation-de-propriete.title: Certificate of ownership: definition
attestation-de-propriete.description: What a certificate of ownership is for and in which situations it may be issued in France.

bail-mobilite.definition: Short-term furnished lease reserved for certain categories of temporary tenants and subject to specific legal conditions.
bail-mobilite.title: Mobility lease (bail mobilité): definition and conditions
bail-mobilite.description: The main features of the French mobility lease and the conditions that apply to it.

bailleur-social.definition: Organisation or entity that offers social rental housing within the rules and missions that apply to it.
bailleur-social.title: Social housing landlord: definition
bailleur-social.description: The role of a social housing landlord in providing social rental homes.

bornage.definition: Procedure that legally fixes the boundary between adjoining plots of land, carried out under the applicable rules and, where required, by a chartered surveyor (géomètre-expert).
bornage.title: Boundary survey (bornage): definition and purpose
bornage.description: What a boundary survey is for and why it can matter before buying or dividing a plot.

budget-acquisition.definition: Overall amount a buyer plans to commit to buy a property, which may include the price, purchase costs, financing costs and planned works.
budget-acquisition.title: Property purchase budget: definition
budget-acquisition.description: How to tell the price of a property from the total budget a purchase really requires.

caution.definition: Person who undertakes, on the terms of the deed, to guarantee the payment of certain sums or the performance of obligations by another person. The word is also commonly used for the guarantee mechanism itself.
caution.title: Guarantor in a rental: definition
caution.description: The role of a guarantor and the difference between a guarantor and a security deposit.

certificat-de-conformite.definition: Expression sometimes used for a document attesting compliance in a given context. In planning, the applicable formalities and documents must be identified precisely, as there is no single certificate for every situation.
certificat-de-conformite.title: Compliance of building works: which documents?
certificat-de-conformite.description: The documents that may come into play after building works and what to check depending on the project.

certificat-urbanisme-operationnel.definition: Planning certificate stating whether a described project can be carried out on a plot in view of the known rules and public utilities, without being a building permit in itself.
certificat-urbanisme-operationnel.title: Detailed planning certificate (CU opérationnel): definition
certificat-urbanisme-operationnel.description: What a detailed planning certificate tells you before you prepare a construction project in France.

charges-recuperables.definition: Expenses the landlord may ask the tenant to reimburse, within the limits and in the manner set by the applicable texts.
charges-recuperables.title: Recoverable charges: definition
charges-recuperables.description: The principle of recoverable charges and the split between landlord expenses and charges payable by the tenant.

clause-penale.definition: Contract clause setting in advance a sum due in the event of non-performance or delay, subject to the review and rules provided for by the applicable law.
clause-penale.title: Penalty clause in real estate: definition
clause-penale.description: The role of a penalty clause in a property contract and why its wording deserves attention.

coefficient-occupation-sols.term: Plot ratio (coefficient d’occupation des sols, COS)
coefficient-occupation-sols.definition: Former planning indicator that capped the buildable floor area in relation to the size of the plot. Its general use was abolished by national reforms, subject to the situations and documents that apply.
coefficient-occupation-sols.title: Plot ratio (COS): definition
coefficient-occupation-sols.description: What the French plot ratio (COS) meant and why current rules must be checked in the applicable planning document.

combles.definition: Space between a building’s top floor and its roof. Depending on its layout, it may be convertible or remain a non-habitable volume.
combles.title: Loft space: definition and conversion potential
combles.description: The difference between convertible and non-convertible loft space and what determines how it can be used.

commission-agence.definition: Remuneration of a real estate professional when the conditions set out in the mandate and by regulation are met. How it is calculated and paid must be specified.
commission-agence.title: Real estate agency commission: definition
commission-agence.description: How an agency commission is defined and where to check the conditions of payment.

compromis-sous-condition.term: Conditional sale agreement (compromis sous condition suspensive)
compromis-sous-condition.definition: Preliminary sale agreement whose final completion depends in particular on one or more conditions set out in the contract being met.
compromis-sous-condition.title: Conditional sale agreement: definition
compromis-sous-condition.description: How conditions precedent can frame a French preliminary sale agreement.

conge-pour-vendre.term: Notice to quit in order to sell (congé pour vendre)
conge-pour-vendre.definition: Notice by which a landlord ends a residential lease in order to sell the home, in the cases and under the forms, time limits and pre-emption rights laid down by law.
conge-pour-vendre.title: Notice to sell (congé pour vendre): definition and general rules
conge-pour-vendre.description: The principle of a landlord’s notice to sell and why the time limits and formalities must be respected.

diagnostic-plomb.definition: Report aimed at identifying the risk of lead exposure from the coatings of certain homes, depending in particular on their construction date and the applicable rules.
diagnostic-plomb.title: Lead survey (CREP): definition and purpose
diagnostic-plomb.description: In which situations a lead survey may be required and what it seeks to identify.

diagnostic-termites.definition: Report checking for termites in the areas and buildings covered by the applicable obligations, which depend in particular on local orders.
diagnostic-termites.title: Termite survey: definition
diagnostic-termites.description: The purpose of a termite survey and why the obligations depend on where the property is located.

division-parcellaire.definition: Operation that divides a landholding into several plots, subject to the applicable formalities and planning rules.
division-parcellaire.title: Land division: definition and steps
division-parcellaire.description: The main checks to carry out before dividing a plot of land into several parcels.

synonyms: Droits de mutation à titre onéreux
droit-de-mutation.definition: Duties and taxes payable on certain transfers of assets or rights, in particular on the sale of a property. The amount depends on the applicable regime and the nature of the transaction.
droit-de-mutation.title: Property transfer duties: definition
droit-de-mutation.description: The role of transfer duties in the purchase costs of a property in France.

encadrement-loyers.definition: Regulatory scheme that limits, in certain areas and under certain conditions, the level or increase of residential rents.
encadrement-loyers.title: Rent control: definition and scope
encadrement-loyers.description: The principle of rent control and why the rules that apply at the home’s address must be checked.

etat-datation.definition: Document prepared by the managing agent when a co-ownership unit is sold, setting out certain financial information on the seller, the unit and the co-ownership, under the applicable rules.
etat-datation.title: État daté: definition in a co-ownership sale
etat-datation.description: The role of the état daté and the financial information it provides when a co-ownership unit is sold.

frais-mainlevee.definition: Fees linked to removing a security registered against a property, when a release is needed and under the applicable formalities.
frais-mainlevee.title: Mortgage release fees: definition
frais-mainlevee.description: When mortgage release fees may arise on a sale or on repaying a loan.

garantie-visale.definition: Rental guarantee scheme offered by Action Logement for tenants and homes that meet its eligibility criteria. The conditions must be checked when applying.
garantie-visale.title: Visale guarantee: definition and conditions
garantie-visale.description: The principle of the Visale rental guarantee and the eligibility conditions to check before signing the lease.

indemnite-immobilisation.definition: Sum provided for in some unilateral promises to sell in return for taking the property off the market during the option period, under the contractual and legal conditions.
indemnite-immobilisation.title: Option fee (indemnité d’immobilisation): definition
indemnite-immobilisation.description: What the option fee is in a French unilateral promise to sell.

loi-pinel.definition: Former tax scheme for buy-to-let investment whose conditions and period of application are set by law. The rules that apply to each investment and its date must be checked.
loi-pinel.title: Pinel scheme: definition and points to watch
loi-pinel.description: The historical principle of the Pinel scheme and why the investment date is key to its tax treatment.

synonyms: Loi pour l’accès au logement et un urbanisme rénové
loi-alur.definition: French law that reformed several aspects of housing, letting, co-ownership and the real estate professions. Its provisions apply according to the texts in force and their amendments.
loi-alur.title: ALUR law: definition and areas covered
loi-alur.description: The main areas covered by the French ALUR law and why the provisions in force must be checked.

loi-hoguet.definition: Law governing certain professional activities relating to property transactions and property management, with obligations attached to carrying out these activities.
loi-hoguet.title: Hoguet law: definition and professional obligations
loi-hoguet.description: The role of the Hoguet law in regulating real estate professionals in France.

mandat-exclusif.definition: Mandate by which the owner entrusts the marketing of the property to a single professional for the period and on the conditions set in the contract.
mandat-exclusif.title: Exclusive sale mandate: definition
mandat-exclusif.description: The principle of an exclusive mandate and the contract terms to examine before signing it.

mandat-simple.definition: Mandate allowing the owner to entrust the marketing of the property to a professional while keeping, subject to the contract, the option of using other agencies or selling privately.
mandat-simple.title: Non-exclusive sale mandate: definition
mandat-simple.description: How a non-exclusive mandate works and how it differs from an exclusive mandate.

offre-achat.definition: Proposal made by a prospective buyer stating in particular the price offered and, where relevant, certain conditions. Its effect depends on its wording, its acceptance and the circumstances.
offre-achat.title: Purchase offer on a property: definition
offre-achat.description: What to state in a purchase offer and the points to watch before sending it.

pret-amortissable.definition: Loan whose capital is repaid gradually with each instalment, usually made up of a capital part and an interest part.
pret-amortissable.title: Repayment (amortising) mortgage: definition
pret-amortissable.description: How a repayment loan works and what monthly instalments are usually made of.

pret-taux-fixe.definition: Loan whose nominal interest rate stays the same for the term set in the contract, subject to the applicable contract terms.
pret-taux-fixe.title: Fixed-rate mortgage: definition
pret-taux-fixe.description: The features of a fixed-rate mortgage and what to compare in a loan offer.

reglement-lotissement.definition: Document that may set rules specific to a housing subdivision, subject to its scope, its duration and the applicable legal rules. It must be distinguished from public planning documents.
reglement-lotissement.title: Subdivision regulations: definition
reglement-lotissement.description: The role of subdivision regulations and the useful checks before buying a plot.

retrait-gonflement-argiles.definition: Phenomenon caused by changes in the volume of certain clay soils depending in particular on their water content, which can lead to ground movement and damage buildings.
retrait-gonflement-argiles.title: Clay shrink-swell: definition
retrait-gonflement-argiles.description: The clay shrink-swell phenomenon and why it matters when assessing the risks of a plot.

syndic-benevole.definition: Co-owner elected to act as managing agent without carrying out this role as a paid professional, under the conditions laid down by regulation.
syndic-benevole.title: Volunteer managing agent: definition and role
syndic-benevole.description: The role of a volunteer managing agent and the responsibilities of running a co-ownership.

tantiemes-copropriete.definition: Share expressing a unit’s portion of the co-ownership, used in particular to split certain charges and to determine voting rights under the applicable rules.
tantiemes-copropriete.title: Co-ownership shares (tantièmes): definition
tantiemes-copropriete.description: What tantièmes represent and their role in splitting charges and in co-ownership votes.

taux-endettement.definition: Ratio between the loan repayments taken into account and the income considered in a borrower’s financial assessment, according to the lender’s criteria.
taux-endettement.title: Debt-to-income ratio for a mortgage: definition
taux-endettement.description: What the debt-to-income ratio means and the other points examined in a mortgage application.

usufruit-temporaire.definition: Right to use a property and receive its income for a fixed period without holding the bare ownership, according to how the right was created.
usufruit-temporaire.title: Temporary usufruct: definition
usufruit-temporaire.description: The principle of temporary usufruct and the difference between usufruct and bare ownership.

vente-aux-encheres-immobilieres.definition: Sale procedure in which candidates place bids under set rules. The terms, effects and safeguards vary depending in particular on whether it is a court-ordered or a notarial sale.
vente-aux-encheres-immobilieres.title: Property auctions: definition
vente-aux-encheres-immobilieres.description: The principles of a property auction and the precautions to take before bidding.
